title: Warming-by-drought evenness intervals crossed zero in four Cedar Creek samples in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether drought changes the warming response of plant biomass evenness at Cedar Creek. We used 432 records from nine whole plots per planting group in 2017-2022. Four paired log-evenness interaction estimates were +0.1743, +0.0395, +0.1032 and -0.1665 for two planting groups and two periods. All four adjusted plot intervals included zero. An exact log split showed that richness and evenness parts had opposite signs in the early 16-species sample. This arithmetic does not identify a mechanism. Single-plot omissions kept three primary signs fixed but did not resolve uncertainty. A bounded-error diagnostic gave sufficient sign-stability factors of 1.010 to 1.045. These are assumed error limits, not measured errors. Moving harvest strips, nine plots per group, one site and reused plots limit inference. We do not establish no interaction, independent regional transfer, or an air pollution effect. Code, aggregate results, exact source hashes, retrieval instructions and independent numerical checks are included. External source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Warming-by-drought contrasts in log evenness. All four Bonferroni plot intervals include zero. The periods reuse plots at one site.
